html:
The ceiling of the pope's chapel in the Vatican, painted in fresco by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512. Pope Julius II gave him the job, though Michelangelo thought of himself as a sculptor, not a painter.

The middle of the ceiling tells nine stories from the Book of Genesis, from the separation of light and darkness to the drunkenness of Noah. The best known is The Creation of Adam, with the two fingers almost touching. Around them sit prophets, sibyls and hundreds of figures, many of them nude, which let Michelangelo show the human body in every pose.

The walls below had already been painted by Botticelli, Perugino and others. Michelangelo came back in the 1530s to paint The Last Judgment behind the altar. The ceiling was copied by artists at once and is still seen as a peak of the High Renaissance. The chapel is also where cardinals meet to elect a new pope.
